Figure 11: Case study: memory-guided regulatory verification. Retrieved experience helps EVONOTE verify clinical-trial, EUA, and safety-review details for a stronger correction. See detailed analysis in §F.5.

Table 1: Effectiveness (%) of note generation on MM-HEALTHCN. “Human Baseline” is the original humanwritten Community Notes. Metrics are relevance after length-validity filtering (R), evidence correctness (C), note helpfulness (H), and pairwise win rate against the Human Baseline (Win.; ties count as 0.5). See §6.1 for setup, §6.2 for variants, and Table 6 for length compliance rates. Best and second-best results are bolded and underlined.

Table 12: Attribution categories of 4,277 Note Writer memories obtained by EVONOTE from MMHEALTHCN. Each memory is assigned to its primary reusable correction strategy, separately for evidence acquisition and note writing. Detailed analysis is in §F.4.
Figure 15: Prompt for the Note Writer agent (§4.4, §B.3.2).

Figure 2: Reusable misinformation correction experience can remain episode-local. (a) Distribution of major correction-relevant claim patterns inferred from helpful-note cases; detailed categories are provided in Table 4. (b) Timeline of one recurring medical mechanism overclaim pattern. Although the earlier Helpful lesson was available before the later posts appeared, later notes miss the same correction strategy and are rated Not Helpful.
